info.title: Eidola API
info.description: Privacy-transparent AI proxy API with inline verification metadata

post.description:
Accepts any active Stripe price ID. Automatically determines whether to
create a subscription or one-time payment checkout based on the price type.
For subscription prices, enforces the one-active-subscription constraint.

get.description:
Always 200 on a reachable Stripe: having no subscription is an answer,
not a failure. The states are distinguished so a client can tell "never
transacted" from "has a payment relationship but nothing in force" —
the second has a billing portal worth offering, the first does not.

post.summary:
POST /v1/account/terms — record acceptance of a current document version
(authenticated).

post.description:
Requires an ACT (Anonymous Credit Token) for authorization. The spend proof
is verified, the nullifier is recorded, and a refund token is issued with
any unspent credits.

200.description: Chat completion response with privacy and verification metadata

post.summary: Recover a refund token for a previously spent ACT.
post.description:
If the ACT's nullifier was already recorded (the server received and
processed the original request), the stored refund token is returned.

If the nullifier was NOT recorded (the original request never arrived),
the server verifies the spend proof, records the nullifier, issues a
full refund (no credits consumed), stores it, and returns it.

In both cases, the client gets a refund token it can combine with its
local `PreRefund` state to reconstruct a credential.

404.description: Nullifier found but refund token not yet available

get.summary: GET /v1/terms — the document versions whose acceptance is required.
get.description:
Public, and necessarily so: a client fetches this *before* it has an
account, to learn what it must accept. It takes no credential and returns
no account-specific data. (Accepting them is `POST /v1/account/terms`,
which is on the linked surface.)

AcceptTermsRequest.description: Acceptance of one currently required document version.

sha256.description:
Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the document text being accepted; must match
the currently required version from `GET /v1/terms`.

AssistantMessage.description: An assistant message in a response.

reasoning_content.description:
Reasoning ("thinking") output from models that emit it. Two
spellings are in the wild: OpenAI o-series and many compatible
gateways use `reasoning_content`; vLLM uses `reasoning`. We
faithfully round-trip whichever the upstream sent so clients can
pick. Both stay `None` for non-thinking models.

tool_calls.description:
Tool calls the model asked for. Relayed to the client **verbatim**
(raw `Value`s) so the ids and any provider extension fields survive —
the client replays these objects unchanged on its follow-up request,
and a narrower struct here would silently drop what it doesn't model,
exactly the defect the `reasoning*` fields above were added to fix.

linkable.description: Whether this authorization method allows linking across requests.

BackendAttestation.description: Backend attestation from the inference provider.

provider.description: The provider that issued the attestation (e.g., "redpill").

signature.description: The ECDSA signature over the signed content.

signing_address.description: The signing address (e.g., Ethereum address for Phala/RedPill).

BalancePool.description: One balance pool: credits sharing an origin and expiration.

amount.description: Credits remaining in this pool (micro-USD denominated).

expires_at.description:
ISO-8601 instant at which these credits expire; absent for credits
that never expire.

source.description: Where the pool came from: `subscription`, `purchase`, or `other`.

BalancesResponse.description:
Credit balance breakdown. All amounts are credits, denominated in
micro-USD (1 credit = $0.000001).

created.description: Unix timestamp of when the chunk was created.

oneOf.description: Usage statistics (included in the final chunk by some providers).

max_completion_tokens.description: The maximum number of completion tokens to generate.

messages.description: A list of messages comprising the conversation.

model.description: ID of the model to use.

oneOf.description: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating.

Streaming options. The OpenAI-compatible field; we accept it for
API parity with clients that already set it (e.g. an SDK setting
`include_usage: true` to capture token counts in the final chunk).
Note: the server overrides `include_usage` to `true` for any
streaming request before forwarding upstream — usage is required
for accurate per-token refunds and isn't a client choice.

tool_choice.description:
How the model should choose among `tools` (`"none"` / `"auto"` /
`"required"`, or a `{"type":"function", …}` object). Opaque
pass-through for the same reason as [`Self::tools`].

tools.description:
Tool (function) definitions the model may call.

**Opaque pass-through.** Each entry is forwarded upstream verbatim:
the server never executes a tool and has no reason to understand the
JSON Schema inside `function.parameters`, while modelling it would
mean rejecting (via this struct's `deny_unknown_fields`) every
provider extension a client legitimately sends. Keeping the entries
as raw `Value`s is also what lets the pricing contract measure
exactly the bytes that go on the wire — see
`handlers::chargeable_prompt_tokens_for`.

created.description: Unix timestamp of when the completion was created.

oneOf.description: The reason the model stopped generating.

ChunkChoice.description: A choice delta in a streaming chunk.

delta.description: The delta (partial update) for this choice.

oneOf.description: The reason the model stopped generating (only in final chunk).

ChunkDelta.description: A delta update in a streaming response.

reasoning_content.description:
Reasoning ("thinking") deltas — same dual spelling as
`AssistantMessage`. Without these fields here, serde silently
drops the upstream `reasoning_content` / `reasoning` keys during
deserialization and the client only ever sees `delta.content`.
Round-trip whatever the upstream emits.

tool_calls.description:
Streamed tool-call deltas, relayed **verbatim** as raw `Value`s.

Nothing about a streamed tool call is guaranteed to arrive whole: the
id, the function name and the `arguments` string all arrive in
fragments keyed by the entry's `index`, and the client reassembles
them. The proxy therefore must not model, reorder, or normalize these
entries — including the streaming-only `index` framing key, which the
client's accumulator needs. Same rule as `reasoning*` above: a field
this struct does not name is dropped on re-serialization.

ContentPart.description: A content part within a multimodal message.

DataExposure.description: Describes a party's visibility into request/response data.

sees.description: What data this party can see (e.g., ["prompt", "response", "token_count"]).

created.description: Unix timestamp of when the completion was created.

model.description: The model that produced the completion.

privacy.description: Privacy metadata describing data exposure and authorization.

oneOf.description: Refund token for unspent credits (only present for ACT-authenticated requests).

EidolaStreamMetadata.description:
Metadata event sent as the final SSE event before [DONE] in streaming responses.

Clients identify this by checking `object == "eidola.chat.completion.metadata"`.
Standard OpenAI clients will ignore it.

id.description: The completion ID this metadata belongs to.

ErrorResponse.description: An error response in OpenAI format, optionally including a refund token.

refund.description:
Refund token for unspent credits (present when an error occurs after
the ACT nullifier has been recorded).

FinishReason.description: The reason the model stopped generating.

detail.description: Optional detail level for the image.

url.description: The URL of the image, or a base64-encoded data URI.

ledger_entry_id.description: The ledger entry ID for this issuance.

IssuerKeyResponse.description: A single issuer public key in the `GET /v1/keys` response.

domain_separator.description: Domain separator used for parameter generation.

public_key.description: Base64url-encoded CBOR public key (compressed Ristretto255 point).

oneOf.description:
The content of the message.

Nullable since tool calling: an assistant message that only called
tools carries `"content": null`. The key is deliberately **always
serialized** (no `skip_serializing_if`) — several chat templates
require it to exist, and clients send the explicit `null` for that
reason, so dropping it on the way upstream would change the request.

name.description: An optional name for the participant.

role.description: The role of the message author.

tool_call_id.description: The id of the tool call this message answers (`role: "tool"` only).

tool_calls.description:
Tool calls the assistant made, replayed by the client verbatim on the
follow-up request.

**Opaque pass-through**, like [`ChatCompletionRequest::tools`]: the
client is required to replay the provider's own call objects
unchanged (ids and any provider extension fields intact), so the
server must not normalize them through a narrower struct.

MessageContent.description: Message content can be a simple string or array of content parts (for multimodal).

context_length.description: Maximum context window size in tokens.

description.description: Short description of the model's capabilities.

pricing.description: Pricing in integer credits per 1k tokens.

ModelPricing.description: Pricing for a model in scaled integer credits per token (or per request).

oneOf.description:
Per-request pricing (for models like Whisper or TTS that charge per request
rather than per token). When present, `per_prompt_token` and
`per_completion_token` are zero.

credits.description:
Credits granted by this plan, denominated in micro-USD
(1 credit = $0.000001). Subscription credits expire at the end of
each billing period; one-time purchase credits expire one year
after purchase.

unit_amount.description: Purchase price in the minor unit of `currency` (e.g. cents for USD).

PrivacyMetadata.description:
Privacy metadata describing how the request was authorized, what data is
visible to which parties, and transport security properties.

data_exposure.description: Which parties can see which data, and under what guarantees.

ProxyAttestation.description: Proxy attestation (placeholder for future TEE deployment).

RefundInfo.description: A refund token issued after spending an ACT.

issuer_key_id.description: The issuer key ID that signed this refund.

RefundRecoveryResponse.description: Response from the refund recovery endpoint.

RequiredDocument.description:
A document whose current version must be accepted before purchases or
credential issuance. `sha256` identifies the exact text (the markdown
source, retrievable at `{url}source.md`), so acceptance binds to
precise words rather than a mutable URL; `version` is the document's
monotonically increasing front-matter version, which orders releases
(accepting version N satisfies any requirement ≤ N).

sha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the exact published document text.

url.description: Where the current text is published.

Role.description: The role of a message author.

ScaledPrice.description:
A price expressed as an integer value with a fixed scale factor.

Actual credits per unit = `value / scale_factor`.

StopSequence.description: Stop sequence can be a single string or array of strings.

include_usage.description:
Include token-usage statistics in the final stream chunk. The
server forces this on for upstream calls so it can compute
accurate refunds; the field exists here only to round-trip
honest clients.

SubscriptionResponse.description:
The account's subscription standing.

The `state` field is the answer; the rest is detail that exists only
where it is meaningful. It is deliberately a three-value state rather
than a present/absent subscription, because "this account has never
transacted" and "this account has a payment relationship but no live
subscription" are different situations and lead to different UI.

current_period_end.description:
End of the current billing period, ISO-8601. Present when `state`
is `active` and Stripe reported one.

id.description:
The in-force subscription's Stripe id. Present exactly when `state`
is `active`.

management_url.description:
A Stripe billing-portal session for this customer. Absent exactly
when `state` is `none` — there is no customer to manage.

state.description:
`none` — the account has no Stripe customer, so it has never
transacted and there is nothing to manage. `inactive` — a customer
exists but holds no subscription in a status Eidola treats as in
force. `active` — a subscription is in force.

"In force" means Stripe status `active`, `trialing`, or `past_due`
— the same set the checkout endpoint refuses to double-subscribe
over, so the two answers cannot disagree.

status.description:
The in-force subscription's raw Stripe status, so a client can show
what it actually is (a `past_due` subscription is in force and
wants attention). Present exactly when `state` is `active`.

TermsResponse.description:
The documents (and versions) whose acceptance the server currently
requires. Empty when no acceptance gate is configured.

client_to_proxy.description: Transport from client to this proxy.

proxy_to_backend.description: Transport from this proxy to the backend.

VerificationMetadata.description: Verification metadata with cryptographic attestations for the proxy and backend.

oneOf.description: Backend attestation (only for TEE-backed models like phala/*).
Proxy attestation (None until the proxy runs in a TEE).

basic.description: Account credentials. Username is the account UUID, password is the secret returned at account creation.

tags.name: Linked
tags.description: Authenticated endpoints tied to a known account (HTTP Basic auth).

tags.name: Unlinked
tags.description: Endpoints authenticated with anonymous credentials — usage cannot be linked back to an account.
